subject: Assurance access constraints and pen-test cadence - MSA security exhibit
messages:
From: Emily Wong <emily.w@clearcare.co>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@clearcare.co, Nadia Patel <nadia.patel@clearcare.co>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify SOC 2 / pen-test expectations for MSA order form

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for sending the MSA and order form. Our security team reviewed the security exhibit and had a few follow-ups before we can move to procurement:

- SOC 2: would you confirm whether Redwood will provide a SOC 2 Type II report and the typical lag (i.e., latest 12-month window)?
- Pen test: we need clarity on whether you allow customer-led penetration tests, or require use of an approved testing vendor. If vendor-approved, can you share the list/process?
- Audit scope: request clarification on inspection rights language — specifically whether inspection is limited to sample-based checks and whether there are any blackout windows for testing production systems.
- Evidence cadence: procurement needs a sample cadence (e.g., weekly snapshots, quarterly packages) and delivery mechanism for evidence (SFTP, shared Drive link, or secure portal).

Attached is our SOC2 request template for reference. Can we get a redline or short answers by end of week? If easier, happy to schedule a 30-min call with our security lead.

Appreciate it —
Emily

Attachment: SOC2-request-template.pdf (stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Wong <emily.w@clearcare.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-13T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify SOC 2 / pen-test expectations for MSA order form

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Legal (Karthik, Laura) and Assurance (Ben) to confirm details. Quick answers up front and then we can either redline or take to a brief call:

- SOC 2: Redwood will provide a SOC 2 Type II report covering the most recent 12-month period where available; if a full Type II for the requested window is not available, we can provide an AICPA bridge letter and our most recent Type II plus statement of scope.

- Pen test: our standard approach is to permit customer-conducted pen tests only if coordinated with our security team and limited to pre-approved staging environments; for production, we require use of an approved third-party vendor or our managed testing window to avoid customer impact. We can share the vendor criteria and an escalation path.

- Audit scope / inspection rights: we typically accept bounded inspection language (sampling bands rather than full forensic inspection) and timeboxed inspection windows. We do not consent to unfettered access to production systems or continuous monitoring; any on-site/privileged access requests go through a separate scoped agreement.

- Evidence cadence: our recommended default is weekly snapshots (operational metrics and token-level anonymized logs) for ongoing monitoring and a quarterly evidence package for compliance-related items (SOC reports, penetration test executive summaries). Delivery is via secure pre-authorized links (we can use a one-time secure S3 URL or a secure portal).

I've attached a short diff that highlights the language we expect to propose back in the exhibit. Karthik / Laura / Ben — please review and add legal/security comments; Emily, if you prefer a live walkthrough, I can book 11/16 or 11/17 for a 30-min slot.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>

Date: 2026-11-14T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify SOC 2 / pen-test expectations for MSA order form

Hannah — forwarding my annotated suggestions inline below (high level):

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 9:12 AM Emily Wong <emily.w@clearcare.co> wrote:
> (see original email)

Legal / suggested language highlights:
- SOC 2: require Redwood to deliver a SOC 2 Type II report or equivalent within 30 days of the customer request, subject to redaction for third-party data. If full Type II is not available, include an attestation and bridge letter. Avoid committing to continuous, live access to SOC artifacts.

- Pen test: propose this clause: "Customer may conduct non-destructive penetration testing on pre-approved staging environments with 72 hours prior notice. Production testing is permitted only via Redwood-approved vendors or through Redwood-managed testing windows; vendor selection will be subject to Redwood's security approval and a mutual scoping agreement." This balances customer needs and risk to multi-tenant infra.

- Inspection rights: change phrase "reasonable access" to "timeboxed, sample-based inspection rights" and add an explicit carve-out for operational continuity (no tests during announced maintenance windows or moments of degraded service).

- Evidence cadence and delivery: we recommend specifying transmission method and retention windows. Example: "Operational evidence (anonymized logs, metrics) will be provided as weekly snapshots for a rolling 90-day window; compliance artifacts (SOC 2 report, pen-test executive summary) will be provided within 10 business days of request via secure pre-authorized link."

- Additional ask: include a short escalation clause tied to SLA credits for remediation timelines if a validated pen-test finds high/critical issues attributable to Redwood.

Ben — confirm the staging constraints and the vendor approval checklist so I can include an explicit list or process. Laura — I kept language intentionally conservative; if customer needs are firm about production testing, we can discuss an accommodation path with additional safeguards.

-Karthik

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Wong <emily.w@clearcare.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify SOC 2 / pen-test expectations for MSA order form — proposed path forward

Emily — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary of proposed path forward and next steps: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood will provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (or AICPA bridge + attestation if Type II for the exact window is unavailable). We will deliver via secure pre-authorized link within 10 business days of a formal request.

2) Pen test: we will accept customer testing on pre-approved staging with 72 hours notice (non-destructive testing only). Production tests are allowed only through Redwood-approved vendors or during Redwood-managed testing windows. Ben will share the vendor approval checklist and staging access rules in the next email.

3) Inspection rights: propose sample-based, timeboxed inspections only; full forensic inspections require a separate scoping addendum and legal approval. We will add explicit blackout/wartime carve-outs for operational continuity.

4) Evidence cadence: default weekly operational snapshots (rolling 90 days) + quarterly compliance bundles. Delivery via secure pre-authorized S3 URLs; if ClearCare requires a different mechanism we can negotiate.

Next steps: 
- Ben to send vendor checklist + staging access rules by EOD 11/16.
- Karthik/Laura to produce a short redline to the security exhibit and return to Emily by 11/17.
- If acceptable, Hannah to schedule a 30-min alignment call 11/18 to finalize and move to procurement.

If that timeline works, I'll also publish a DocuSign proposal for the narrow exhibit redline so procurement can mark the order form as ready once legal approves.

Thanks —
Hannah
